WHY PORT 13378?

On its own, ABS listens on port 80. Inside a pod every container shares one network, so two apps can't both have the same port, and a rootless container can't have 80 anyway. The container is started with PORT=13378, and the pod publishes 13378 to the LAN.

HOW IT READS A BOOK

ABS treats each folder as one book. A tidy layout is Author / Book Title / files, with a series folder in between if you like: Author / Series / Book 1 Title / files. One file or fifty MP3 parts, it's all one book to ABS, and chapters come from the file or the parts.

It then looks up covers, descriptions and narrators from online sources and saves what it finds in its own metadata folder, because the library is read-only.

WHAT LIVES WHERE

FOLDERHOLDS
/srv/stream/abs/configDatabase: users, libraries, listening progress, bookmarks
/srv/stream/abs/metadataCovers, cached items, ABS's own backups
/media (read-only)Every drive, so libraries can point anywhere on them

THE TWO LOCKS

From outside, books. is a station floor: the gate's sign-in first, then ABS's own login. At home and over WireGuard the gate skips its sign-in, and you meet ABS's login directly. The ABS login is what keeps each listener's progress their own.

WHO'S THE ROOT?

The very first visit creates the root user, the top admin. Everyone else gets a normal user under Settings → Users.

CLAUDE-VIPERThe books are never touched. ABS only reads them and writes its notes in its own folders on the SSD. Wipe ABS and the library is still sitting there, safe on dock1a.

A TIDY SHELF

audiobooks/
  Author Name/
    Standalone Title/
      book.m4b
    Series Name/
      Book 1 - First Title/
        01.mp3  02.mp3  03.mp3

One folder per book, under its author, with an optional series folder. A single .m4b with built-in chapters or a pile of numbered MP3s: both are one book to ABS.

JOE SABOTAGE REPORT

From manual 3.8 and the stream pod's wiring.

THE ROOT GRAB

The first person to open ABS becomes root. Leave it unclaimed and that could be anyone on the LAN.Create root from the-box as soon as the container first starts.

THE PORT 80 HABIT

Guides on the internet run ABS on port 80. In the shared pod, and rootless, it can't have 80.Keep PORT=13378 in the container and 13378 in pod.sh and nftables.

THE UPLOAD WALL

The library is mounted read-only, so anything that writes into the book folders, like the web Upload page or saving covers next to the files, can't.Add books by copying them over the share from the-box. ABS keeps its own covers in its metadata folder.

THE LOOSE FILES

Fifty MP3s dumped straight into audiobooks/ become fifty "books", or one mess.One folder per book: Author / Title / files.

THE GHOST DRIVE

dock1a unplugged and plugged back: ABS still sees the empty folder from before, and its library looks gone.podman pod restart stream, then scan the library.

THE WRONG TYPE

ABS libraries are either Book or Podcast. Pick Podcast for audiobooks and nothing lines up.Both libraries here are type Book.

THE SHARED ACCOUNT

Two people on one ABS user overwrite each other's progress: you'll resume at chapter 20 of a book you were on chapter 3 of.One ABS user per listener.

THE DOUBLE LOGIN SURPRISE

From outside you sign in at the gate, then ABS asks again. That's normal: ABS doesn't read the gate's sign-in the way Navidrome does.Nothing to fix in the browser. For the phone app away from home, use WireGuard, which skips the gate's sign-in.

LIBRARIAN'S CHECKLIST

  • root user made from the-box
  • Audiobooks library on /media/dock1a/audiobooks
  • Books library on /media/dock1a/books
  • One user per listener, app on each phone
CLAUDE-VIPERMost ABS trouble is folders, not software. Get the shelf tidy and the rest takes care of itself.

KAVITA

The Comics Shop: comics, manga and graphic novels at comics.songofeo.com

Kavita is the island's comic shop. It shelves your CBZ and CBR comic archives, manga and graphic novels by series, draws the covers, and opens a fast page-turning reader right in the browser, phone or tablet included.

It remembers where each reader stopped in every issue, shows what's next in a series, and speaks OPDS, the common catalog language that many reading apps understand. It reads EPUB and PDF too, so it can double as an e-book reader.

Kavita lives in the stream pod on port 5000. Its database, covers and settings stay in /srv/stream/kavita on the SGIN's SSD; the comics come in read-only from dock1a/comics.

CLAUDE-VIPERKA-POW! Every issue from the footlockers, filed, sorted and readable from the couch. The Joes can keep their crumpled paper copies.

SERIES FOLDERS

Kavita groups by series, and it expects the files inside folders under the library root, not loose in it. The safe layout is one folder per series:

comics / Series Name / Series Name 001.cbz

The folder and file names give Kavita its first guess; a ComicInfo.xml inside the archive, when there is one, gives it the real details.

THE LIBRARY TYPE MATTERS

When you add a library, its type (Comic, Manga, Book and so on) tells Kavita how to read names and how to show the pages. The island's library is Comics, type Comic, on /media/dock1a/comics. Manga could get its own library of type Manga later.

WHAT LIVES WHERE

FOLDERHOLDS
/srv/stream/kavita (as /kavita/config)Database, users, reading progress, cover images, logs
/media (read-only)Every drive; the library points at dock1a/comics

WATCHING FOR NEW ISSUES

Kavita watches the library folder and notices new files on its own, and it also rescans on a schedule. Linux limits how many folders one user may watch; part 3.3 raised that limit for podsvc, because Kavita, Jellyfin, ABS and the Navidromes all watch at once.

THE ADMIN

The first visit registers the admin account (the email can be anything local). After that, the admin adds or invites one user per reader.

ROMM

The Arcade: your ROM library, playable in a browser, at arcade.songofeo.com

RomM is the browser arcade. It catalogs every ROM by platform, fetches box art and titles, and with EmulatorJS built in, lets anyone you've signed in play right in their browser. Press start on a laptop, a tablet, even a phone.

The trick: the game runs in the player's browser, not on the server. The SGIN only hands out files, so ten people playing ten games barely tickle its CPU. RomM keeps its catalog in a MariaDB database (next chapter) and its covers and settings on the SGIN's SSD.

The ROMs live on dock1b, in dock1b/roms. Their main copy is on the cabinet, cobra-arcade's D:\Roms, and the cabinet sends them up every night, so the web arcade keeps working while the cabinet sleeps.

TWO ARCADES, ONE ROM PILE

The cabinet (OptiPlex, LaunchBox and RetroArch) plays from D:\Roms with the Tankstick. Its saves live on the cabinet.
The web arcade (RomM and EmulatorJS) plays the nightly copy on dock1b in any browser. Its saves live in RomM, per user.

Examples from the manual: roms/snes, roms/n64, roms/arcade. RomM needs its own names for platforms; the cabinet's folder map translates where the cabinet's names differ.

PRO TIP: GAMEPADS

HOW IT WORKSLEVEL MAP

FROM CABINET TO BROWSER

1 CABINETD:\Roms\<platform>
▶
2 NIGHTLYrobocopy to \\cobra-stream\roms
▶
3 DOCK1Broms/<platform>/
▶
4 ROMMscan, art, :8080
▶
5 BROWSEREmulatorJS plays it

ONE FOLDER PER PLATFORM

RomM expects roms/<platform>/: roms/snes, roms/n64, roms/arcade and so on. Each folder shows up as a platform after a scan. The cabinet's own folder names don't always match RomM's, so the cabinet script 03-roms-map.ps1 writes a folder map, and romm-platforms.sh adds it to RomM's config.yml under system:.

ONE-WAY TRAFFIC

The nightly copy runs cabinet to SGIN only (robocopy /E /XO: adds and updates, never deletes). New ROMs go onto the cabinet's D:\Roms; the next night they appear on dock1b, then a RomM scan picks them up.

WHY RomM MAY WRITE

Unlike the read-only media apps, RomM's roms folder is mounted writable, with keep-groups so it keeps podsvc's media group. No :Z on it, because Samba shares the same folder for the cabinet's copy.

WHAT LIVES WHERE

FOLDERHOLDS
romm/resourcesFetched covers and screenshots
romm/assetsUploaded saves, states, screenshots
romm/configconfig.yml: netplay, folder map
romm/redisIts built-in task queue's data
romm/dbMariaDB's files (romm-db)

SECRETS, NOT SCRIPTS

The database password and RomM's auth key are made once and kept as podman secrets (romm-db-password, romm-auth-secret) when built by the scripts. They never appear in the script or in podman inspect. In Quadlet mode they're in the 600-protected romm*.container files instead.

THE SCOREBOARD IS ELSEWHERE

The hiscore board at scores.songofeo.com runs on the gate, not here. RomM is just the arcade floor.

THE NIGHTLY COPY

On the cabinet, 02-nightly.ps1 sets up the nightly job (run it once with -RunNow for the first copy). It logs to C:\Cobra\nightly-copy.log and writes === end when done. The copy logs in to the SGIN's Samba as user arcade, saved once with cmdkey.

ROMM-DB

The Arcade's memory: a MariaDB database only RomM talks to

Every arcade needs someone keeping the books. romm-db is a MariaDB database server, and it remembers everything RomM knows: which games exist on which platform, their titles and metadata, the users, and who played what.

It has no web page and no public name. It sits in the stream pod, listening on MariaDB's port 3306 on 127.0.0.1, which only containers inside the pod can reach. That port is not in the pod's published list, so nothing on the LAN can talk to it, let alone the internet.

Its files live in /srv/stream/romm/db on the SGIN's SSD. The ROMs themselves aren't in it: the database holds the catalog, the drive holds the games.

CLAUDE-VIPERThe quiet operative. No page, no port to the LAN, no fame. Just a perfect memory. Every good Cobra unit needs one.

HOW IT GETS ITS PASSWORDS

On the very first start, with an empty db folder, MariaDB creates the romm database and user with the password it's given (MARIADB_PASSWORD) and sets the root password. After that, the password is stored inside the database files. Changing the variable later doesn't change it.

With the scripts, the passwords come from podman secrets, handed in as environment variables only inside the container. With the manual's Quadlets, they're written into romm-db.container, which is chmod 600.

THE HEALTH CHECK

The script gives the container a health check (healthcheck.sh --connect --innodb_initialized) and waits for healthy before starting RomM. In Quadlet mode, romm.container says Requires=romm-db.service and After= it instead, so systemd starts the database first.

WHY NOT THE GATE'S DB?

The gate's Postgres belongs to Paperless and lives on another machine. RomM wants MariaDB or MySQL, and keeping its database next to it in the same pod means the arcade never depends on the gate being up.

TIPS & TRICKS

CODES

SGIN · podsvc podman ps --filter name=romm romm-db and romm, both Up. podman logs --tail 30 romm-db podman secret ls Scripts mode: lists the secret names, never the values. podman secret inspect --showsecret --format '{{.SecretData}}' romm-db-password Prints the password. Only when you need it, and not on a shared screen.

PRO TIP: A SPARE COPY

A dump is a plain-text copy of the whole database you can restore from. Inside the container the password is already in the environment, so the dump command doesn't need you to type it:

CODES

SGIN · podsvc podman exec romm-db sh -c 'mariadb-dump -u romm -p"$MARIADB_PASSWORD" romm' > ~/romm-db.sql Writes ~/romm-db.sql in podsvc's home. Move it to dock1a/backups if you want it kept.

PRO TIP: IT'S IN THE BACKUP

/srv/stream is the SGIN's app data. Back it up with RomM stopped (or use a dump), so the database files are consistent.

CLAUDE-VIPERLose the database and RomM forgets its users and saves list, but not a single ROM: those sit safe on dock1b, and a rescan rebuilds the catalog.

JOE SABOTAGE REPORT

Includes a trap that hit the gate's Postgres for real on 6 November 2026.

THE CHOWN DISASTER

On the gate, re-running a chown -R podsvc: /srv/gate after Postgres had made its files broke them ("pg_filenode.map: Permission denied"). Rootless database files belong to a mapped user ID inside the container, not podsvc. The same move on /srv/stream would break romm-db.Never chown -R a database folder. If it happened, repair from podsvc with podman unshare chown -R to the database's own user (999:999 for these official images).

THE NEW-PASSWORD TRAP

Rebuild RomM with fresh random passwords while romm/db still holds the old database: the database keeps the old password, RomM sends the new one, and gets "access denied".Reuse the old values (ROMM_DB_PASSWORD=... ./romm.sh), read from the old romm.container or the saved secret.

THE PERMISSION LOOP

A container that keeps restarting with Permission denied in its log: the image switched to a non-root user inside, and its folder belongs to someone else.Manual 3.8's last bullet: find the user with podman exec <name> id and add UserNS=keep-id:uid=...,gid=....

THE BIG-JUMP UPGRADE

The image is pinned to mariadb:11, so updates stay within MariaDB 11. Changing the tag to a new major version blindly can leave the files needing an upgrade step.Dump first, read the release notes, then change the tag.

THE PUBLISHED DATABASE

Adding 3306 to the pod's published ports "to look at it from the-box" would put a database on the LAN.Leave it out. Use podman exec -it romm-db mariadb -u romm -p romm on the SGIN instead.

THE IMPATIENT START

RomM started before the database was ready fails its first connection. Usually it just retries.The script waits for healthy; in Quadlet mode systemd's After= orders them. Still stuck: podman logs romm-db.

THE PASSWORD ON SCREEN

--showsecret prints the real password in the terminal and in scrollback.Run it only when needed, then clear the screen. Keep a copy in Vaultwarden.

DATABASE KEEPER'S CHECKLIST

  • romm-db Up, before romm
  • Password saved in Vaultwarden
  • 3306 never published
  • No chown -R on /srv/stream/romm/db, ever

ICECAST

The Transmitter: the tower every radio listener tunes in to

Icecast is the radio tower of Song of Eo Radio. It doesn't pick songs and it doesn't play anything by itself. It takes one live audio stream in from the DJ and hands copies out to every listener who tunes in.

The DJ is the next chapter's container, radio (Liquidsoap), which connects to Icecast with a source password and pushes an endless MP3 stream to the mount point /stream. Listeners open http://10.6.9.20:8000/stream at home, or https://radio.songofeo.com/stream through the gate, in a browser, VLC or a radio app.

Icecast is part of manual part 8, the landing site and radio. It joins the stream pod on port 8000, which needs adding to the pod's published ports and to the SGIN's nftables list. It keeps no data folder at all: everything it knows comes from its settings.

CLAUDE-VIPERThis is Cobra Island broadcasting on all frequencies! Well, on one mount point, to at most 50 listeners, behind a login. Still counts.

THREE PASSWORDS

  • Source: what the DJ uses to push audio in. The radio container gets the same one.
  • Admin: for Icecast's admin pages (listeners, kicking a source).
  • Relay: for other Icecast servers relaying this one. Unused here, but set.

With the scripts they're generated once as podman secrets (icecast-source-password and friends). With the manual's Quadlets they're random values written into icecast.container, chmod 600.

THROUGH THE GATE

Manual 8.3 gives radio. its own nginx server block. location / asks Authelia (password only, one_factor), turns buffering off so audio flows straight through, and allows a listener to stay tuned for 24 hours. location /admin allows only 10.6.9.0/24 and 10.6.99.0/24.

WHY BEHIND A LOGIN?

Streaming music you don't hold the rights to, to anyone on the internet, needs public-performance licences, even for a tiny station. So radio. stays behind the gate's sign-in for you and the people you add. Fully public only with music you have rights to: your own, Creative Commons or royalty-free (manual 8.4).

TIPS & TRICKS

PRO TIP: LAN TEST

On the-box, open http://10.6.9.20:8000/stream in VLC (Media → Open Network Stream) or the browser. Music = Icecast and the DJ both work. Silence or 404 = the DJ isn't connected.

PRO TIP: THE STATUS PAGE

http://10.6.9.20:8000/ shows Icecast's status page: the mount, what's playing and how many are listening.

PRO TIP: UPLOAD MATH

Each listener at 192 kb/s uses about 0.2 Mb/s of Xfinity upload. Ten listeners, about 2 Mb/s.

THE PIRATE STATION

THE CLOSED FIREWALL

THE FULL HOUSE

Listener 51 gets turned away: ICECAST_MAX_CLIENTS=50. Your upload speed runs out long before that matters.Raise it only if the upload can carry it.

RADIO

The AutoDJ: Liquidsoap shuffles the music, all day, every day

Meet the DJ who never sleeps. The radio container runs Liquidsoap, a programming language made for radio. Its script, apps/radio/radio.liq, is fifteen lines long: shuffle the music folder, crossfade between songs, never go silent, send it to Icecast.

The container reads the music library read-only, at /media/music, which is dock1a/music on the SGIN, the same folder the Commander's Navidrome reads. It runs the script from /srv/stream/radio/radio.liq (mounted read-only too), encodes MP3 at 192 kb/s, and pushes it to Icecast at 127.0.0.1:8000, mount /stream.

The station's name comes from the environment: RADIO_NAME="Song of Eo Radio". The music folder can be changed the same way with RADIO_MUSIC.

CLAUDE-VIPERNo playlists to build, no requests to take, no coffee breaks. Drop a song into the library and it joins the rotation by itself.

STARTING ORDER

The DJ needs the tower. With the scripts, radio.sh starts Icecast, waits for port 8000, then starts radio. With Quadlets, radio.container has Requires=icecast.service and After= it, plus Restart=on-failure every 10 seconds, so a radio that started too early just tries again.

THE ENTRYPOINT

The Liquidsoap image needs to be told which program to run. The script mode passes --entrypoint liquidsoap and then /radio/radio.liq. In Quadlet mode, if the log says it can't run /radio/radio.liq as a command, the line must be Exec=liquidsoap /radio/radio.liq.

WHERE ITS SETTINGS COME FROM

  • RADIO_MUSIC: folder to shuffle (default /media/music)
  • RADIO_NAME: the station name listeners see
  • ICECAST_SOURCE_PASSWORD: shared with Icecast

WHAT IT PLAYS

All of dock1a/music: the Commander's and Rachel's music both. Comedy and your recorded sessions live in their own folders, so they never get on the air.

WHAT IT DOESN'T DO (YET)

No station IDs, no requests, no schedule. That's the whole point of the fifteen-line script: easy to read, easy to change. Liquidsoap can do all of those later if the Commander wants them.

UP-ALL SKIPS IT

sgin/up-all.sh runs radio.sh only if /srv/stream/radio/radio.liq exists. No script in place, no radio, and the rest of the pod still starts: "skipping the radio (no ... yet, part 8)".

NO PORT, NO DATA

radio has no port of its own and writes nothing. Its only output goes over 127.0.0.1 to Icecast, inside the pod.

CLAUDE-VIPERTower and DJ, two containers, one job each. If the music stops, ask the DJ (podman logs radio). If nobody can hear it, ask the tower.

THE HOUSE BAND

radio. streams the shuffle to anyone signed in at the gate.
music. lets you pick songs yourself, from the same folder.
The website's players on songofeo.com use the floors behind the gate's sign-in.

BONUS STAGE · NOT IN ANY POD

PI-HOLE ×2

The island's phone book, and the ad blocker in front of it

Before your browser can knock on the gate, it has to ask "where is music.songofeo.com?" On Cobra Island, two Pi-holes answer that question for every machine, block the ad and tracker names, and send the rest up to OPNsense.

Neither Pi-hole is a container in this guide's pods. Pi-hole #1 is a small Proxmox container, CT 101 cobra-pihole-1 at 10.6.9.3 on the Latitude. Pi-hole #2 is installed natively on the SGIN at 10.6.9.20, right beside the stream pod. OPNsense's DHCP hands every machine both addresses, so if one goes down for an update, the other keeps answering.

Their best trick is the wildcard: any name under songofeo.com gets answered with 10.6.9.10, the gate. At home your phone never goes out to the internet and back to reach your own server; it walks straight down the hall. That's why the floors open without the sign-in at home: the gate sees a 10.6.9.x address, and Authelia lets home addresses through.

BONUS STAGEVIPER VISIONYOU AND YOUR POD!
HOW IT WORKSTHREE MAGIC LINES

THE DNSMASQ LINES (SAME ON BOTH)

  • address=/*.songofeo.com/10.6.9.10: every name under songofeo.com goes to the gate. The *. leaves the bare songofeo.com alone, so the station on Porkbun's hosting still loads at home.
  • server=/www.songofeo.com/#: www is the station too, so it's passed up to the real DNS.
  • server=/vpn.songofeo.com/#: the WireGuard endpoint. It must be your public address even at home, or a laptop that sets up its tunnel at home would point it at the gate.

SHORT NAMES

Both Pi-holes carry the same 8 host entries, each with a full and a short name: cobra-firewall .1, cobra-command .2, cobra-pihole-1 .3, cobra-switch .5, cobra-ap .6, cobra-gate .10, cobra-stream .20, cobra-arcade .30.

The short ones matter over WireGuard: a VPN client doesn't get the home.arpa search suffix, so \\cobra-stream would otherwise not resolve.

WHY "ALL" IS SAFE HERE

Pi-hole's default LOCAL mode ignores clients on subnets it has no interface on, and WireGuard's 10.6.99.0/24 is one of those. So both run listeningMode ALL. That's safe because nothing outside reaches them: CT 101 sits only on the LAN, and the SGIN's nftables lets port 53 in from the LAN and WireGuard only.

HOW MACHINES FIND THEM

OPNsense runs Dnsmasq DNS & DHCP. Its DHCP option 6 (DNS servers) hands out 10.6.9.3, 10.6.9.20, with the domain home.arpa. A machine that renews its lease gets both.

WHERE THE REST GOES

Names that aren't blocked and aren't local go up to OPNsense at 10.6.9.1, whose Unbound resolver sends them out over DNS over TLS. Your ISP sees an encrypted stream, not your lookups.

CODES: ASK THE PHONE BOOK

THE-BOX · PowerShell nslookup tv.songofeo.com 10.6.9.3 Must answer 10.6.9.10. nslookup tv.songofeo.com 10.6.9.20 Same answer from Pi-hole #2. nslookup vpn.songofeo.com 10.6.9.3 Must be your public IP, never 10.6.9.10. nslookup songofeo.com 10.6.9.3 Porkbun's address: the station has to load at home too.

TIPS & TRICKS

PRO TIP: SYNC THE TWINS

Change blocklists on Pi-hole #1, then copy them across: #1 → Settings → Teleporter → Export, and #2 → Teleporter → Import. Do it on the-box.

PRO TIP: SITE BROKEN?

Query Log on either admin page, filter by your machine, reload the site. Blocked names show in red.

CODES

THE-BOX · PowerShell ipconfig /renew ipconfig /all DNS Servers must list 10.6.9.3 and 10.6.9.20, suffix home.arpa.

CODES

SGIN · eels pihole status sudo pihole -up Update #2, check it answers, then do #1 (pct enter 101 on cobra-command). While one restarts, machines ask the other. sudo pihole setpassword Forgot the admin password? Set a new one.

PRO TIP: XFINITY WI-FI

Xfinity's router has no NAT loopback, so songofeo names don't load from the Xfinity Wi-Fi. Use the WireGuard home profile (endpoint 10.0.0.2:51820) until the cobra access point arrives.

JOE SABOTAGE REPORT

THE GREEDY WILDCARD

The wildcard also grabbed vpn., which must stay public for WireGuard.The server=/vpn.songofeo.com/# line on both Pi-holes passes it up.

THE SILENT DHCP

OPNsense's Dnsmasq had no DNS option at all, so every machine got 10.6.9.1 and skipped the Pi-holes.DHCP option 6 = 10.6.9.3, 10.6.9.20.

THE STATIC DESKTOP

the-box had a hand-typed IP with one DNS server and no suffix, so short names never resolved.Switched to DHCP with a reservation at .50.

THE VPN THAT EATS DNS

PIA VPN on the-box takes over DNS and reconnects by itself, so lookups skip the Pi-holes.Disconnect PIA before testing anything DNS.

THE MISSING TWIN ENTRIES

Pi-hole #1 was missing cobra-switch and cobra-ap while #2 had all 8, so a name worked or failed depending on which twin your machine asked.Both now carry the same 8 hosts. Change one, change the other the same day (Settings → Local DNS Records, or Teleporter).

LETTERS FROM THE BARRACKS
Why do I sign in once on my phone, but my TV never asks?
tv. is the one floor nginx sends straight to Jellyfin without Authelia, because TV apps can't show a web sign-in page. Jellyfin's own login guards it instead.
At home nothing asks me to sign in. Is that a hole?
No. The floors trust home (10.6.9.x) and WireGuard (10.6.99.x) addresses. The admin apps still ask for password and TOTP, even at home.
Can I just open a port to Jellyfin on the SGIN?
Please don't. Everything on the SGIN answers without the gate. Exactly one forward lives on OPNsense: WAN 443 to 10.6.9.10.
How do I give a friend Jellyfin?
On the-box, Jellyfin → Dashboard → Users → add them, with only the libraries you want. Then send them https://tv.songofeo.com. No gate account needed.
The gate rebooted but the SGIN was off. Now what?
Paperless, MeTube and eo-art can't find their shared folder and fail. systemd retries them every minute, so they come back by themselves once the SGIN is up.
Where do my passwords live?
Yours: in Vaultwarden at vault., LAN and WireGuard only. The apps' generated ones: as podman secrets, readable with the codes on the previous page. Never in the scripts.
How do I know when something breaks?
Uptime Kuma at status. watches every app, and Homepage at command. shows a live dot on each tile.
Who gets in through the gate sign-in?
Whoever is in Authelia's users.yml on the gate. Right now that's eels and rachel.
